Establish what the BJP resolution actually commits the party to and over what period, what the Congress Working Committee decided that triggered it, what Gandhi actually wrote about the song being an 'anti-imperialist cry' and in what context (the BJP is quoting him against his own 1937 position — say so), what Tharoor said, what legal status each text holds, and where singing it has already been made compulsory in schools or assemblies. Who bears the cost: Indian Muslims, for whom a compulsory recitation is a devotional act, and who did not ask for the question to be reopened. All three sources are Indian (HT, TOI, NDTV) with divergence 0.36 — NDTV is markedly the most favourable at 0.44; attribute framings and carry the historical record independently.

stories.label: AJK PM Rathore urges dialogue to resolve AJK crisis, calls for end to 'base camp' mindset
stories.summary: The prime minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is asking Islamabad to stop treating the territory as a 'base camp' — a phrase that carries the entire constitutional problem in two words. Lead with what 'base camp' means and why an AJK premier saying it out loud is the news: AJK is administered as a staging ground for a claim on the whole of Kashmir rather than as a place where four million people live, which is why its budget, its electricity tariff and its wheat subsidy are set outside it and why the Joint Awami Action Committee's shutter-down movement has been about flour and power bills rather than about the dispute. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry: a territory held for its symbolic value in an inter-state claim gets governed in the register of that claim, so ordinary administrative grievances have no ordinary channel and escalate straight to general strikes. Establish what the JAAC has demanded and what was conceded in earlier rounds and then not implemented, why the committee is proscribed and under what law, what powers the AJK Council and the Kashmir Affairs ministry hold over an elected AJK government, how many have been killed or detained in the protests, the price of subsidised flour and the electricity tariff at the centre of it, and when the incoming government takes office. Who bears the cost: AJK residents paying for hydropower generated in their own valleys. Pakistan is an OIC state and Dawn (PK) is the regional source, reporting on the record from Muzaffarabad. Fills the Asia gap the audit has flagged.

stories.label: CWPPF demands independent probe into police assault on Abuja journalist
stories.summary: A press-freedom coalition is demanding that the Abuja journalist's assault be investigated 'under an independent mechanism outside the direct command structure implicated in the allegation' — and that clause, not the assault, is the story. Lead with it: the request concedes that Nigeria's standing remedy, an internal police investigation, cannot produce a finding against the command that ordered the act, so the coalition is asking for a body that does not currently exist. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry beyond Nigeria: where the only investigator of police violence is the police, the recorded outcome of every such case is 'no case', and the resulting statistics then get cited as evidence the problem is rare — the absence of findings is manufactured by the structure, not by the facts. Establish who the journalist is, what happened at Lugbe and when, what injuries and what was seized, which unit is implicated, what the Inspector-General and the Police Service Commission have said, what the PSC's actual powers are and how many officers it has disciplined for assaulting journalists in the past five years, and how many Nigerian journalists were attacked by security forces in the last year. Who holds power: the IGP choosing the forum; who bears the cost: reporters covering the capital. Nigeria is an OIC member and Premium Times (NG) is the regional source, doing original accountability reporting — attribute the coalition's characterisation to the coalition.

stories.label: Canada vows 'dollar-for-dollar' response to Trump tariffs
stories.summary: Talks collapsed in Washington on Friday, 50% US tariffs took effect, and Carney will retaliate dollar-for-dollar from September 8 — but the load-bearing detail is what Canada turned down. Greer says the US offered to cut tariffs on steel, aluminium and autos and scrap the lumber tariff, and Ottawa still walked; lead with the fact that a government refused tariff relief, because that tells you the disputed term was not the rate but something structural it would not sign. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry: 'dollar-for-dollar' is a deliberate arithmetic, not rhetoric — a smaller economy cannot match a larger one proportionally, so it matches in absolute dollars and targets the goods where the political pain lands hardest per dollar. That is the standard playbook for every middle economy facing a tariff wall, and it is why retaliation lists read like electoral maps. Establish what the 50% tariff covers and what share of Canadian exports it hits, exactly what Greer says was offered and what Ottawa says was actually on the table, what Canada's retaliation list contains and its dollar value, when each side's measures bite, what USMCA obligations both are now breaching and what remedy the agreement provides, and the integrated auto and energy supply chains that cross the border multiple times per vehicle. Who bears the cost: workers in Ontario and Michigan plants on the same production line. Multi-source with unusual breadth — CBC (CA), Fortune (US), NYT (US), TRT World (TR), India Today (IN), Al Jazeera (QA), Dawn (PK); divergence 0.20, with Al Jazeera and CBC most positive on Carney and Fortune flat. This also carried 353 points on Hacker News, a public-attention signal from our technical readership.

stories.label: Iran warns neighbours over US pressure as Hormuz tensions spread
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, is threatening Iran's own neighbours against joining the US economic campaign — while France and Saudi Arabia work on energy routes that bypass Hormuz entirely. Lead with the pairing, because the two halves are the same event seen from either end: Tehran's remaining leverage is the strait, and every bypass pipeline built now is a permanent subtraction from that leverage that no ceasefire returns. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — chokepoint power is a depreciating asset. Threatening to close a strait raises the return on every alternative route, so the threat finances its own obsolescence: East-West and Petroline capacity, the Fujairah and Yanbu terminals, and any new French-Saudi arrangement are all bought with money that Iranian pressure justified. Establish exactly what Rezaei said and to whom, in what forum, and what Mehr's parallel account of the same interview adds about 'reforms in Iran's diplomatic behaviour' (the same man, the same broadcast, a notably different emphasis for the domestic audience — contrast them directly). Then the hard numbers: which Gulf states have joined the US pressure track and what they host, existing bypass capacity in barrels per day against Hormuz throughput, what France and Riyadh are actually discussing, where Brent sits, and what Egypt's move to seek US talks signals. Who bears the cost: the Gulf and South Asian importers who pay the war-risk premium either way. Iran is an OIC state — Mehr News (IR) merged in as the regional and Iranian-state account of the same remarks; treat it as an interested party, attribute both accounts, and anchor the threat's wording on the direct quote. Continues the Hormuz arc at the leverage-decay link, distinct from the throughput and importer-balance-sheet entries.

stories.label: 'Orcas' with likely inside info win big on Trump Jr.-funded Polymarket
stories.summary: A research group has identified 152 Polymarket wallets with a 97.2% success rate that collectively won $8 million betting on US military operations, including the June 2025 strikes on Iran. Lead with the win rate, because it is the argument: 97.2% is not skill in a binary market, it is foreknowledge, and the number is derivable by anyone because the ledger is public. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — a prediction market on military action converts operational secrecy into a priced, publicly readable signal. Unusual position-building becomes an indicator of an imminent operation, so the market is simultaneously an insider-trading venue and an open-source intelligence feed; ACDC's co-founder says as much, and it would be strange if foreign services were not reading it. Establish exactly what the Anti-Corruption Data Collective measured and over what period, the Van Dyke case (a master sergeant charged over $400,000 in bets on the Venezuela operation, who has pleaded not guilty — say so), the repeated pre-announcement bets on crude falling before Iran-talks statements, who at Polymarket is connected to whom (Trump Jr. as adviser, 1789 Capital as investor) and what the family's separate drone and defence holdings are, what the March White House guidance actually prohibits and with what penalty, and where the Senate's self-ban and Torres's House bill stand. Who holds power: officials who can move a market by acting; who bears the cost: the operational security of the personnel carrying out the missions. SOURCING: Responsible Statecraft is advocacy-adjacent and must not supply the framing — the underlying reporting is Reuters on a named ACDC report, and the article should be anchored on Reuters, the ACDC findings and the charging documents. Every claim about the Trump family's holdings must be attributed to Reuters, not asserted.

stories.label: Spatiotemporal distribution and evolution mechanisms of land subsidence in areas with combined coal mining and groundwater extraction
stories.summary: A study separates how much of the ground's sinking comes from coal mining and how much from pumping the aquifer, in places doing both at once. Lead with why the separation matters rather than the subsidence itself: mining subsidence is compensable and attributable to a licensed operator, while groundwater subsidence is diffuse, largely irreversible, and legally nobody's — so the ratio between them decides who pays for a cracked house, and until now the two were measured as one number. Teach the mechanism: coal extraction removes a seam and the roof collapses into it, a fast and localised failure; groundwater withdrawal compacts clay layers between aquifers, which is slow, regional, and permanent because the pore structure does not re-expand when the water returns. Establish which basin and which years the study covers, the method (InSAR time series, and say plainly what it can and cannot resolve), the measured subsidence rates and the attributed split, where the two drivers compound rather than add, and what the authors recommend. Then the part our reader should carry outward: the same combination is running under Shanxi and Inner Mongolia, under the Indo-Gangetic plain, and around Iranian and North African cities where aquifer depletion has already opened fissures — Iran's own subsidence is among the fastest measured anywhere. This is an early-access accepted manuscript; say so, and give the DOI.

stories.label: Computer models pinpoint catalysts for replacing fossil-fueled ammonia production
stories.summary: Computational screening has identified candidate catalysts that could make ammonia without the fossil-fuelled Haber-Bosch process — the single industrial reaction that consumes up to 2% of world energy and emits about 1.5% of global greenhouse gases. Lead with what ammonia actually is in the world: it is the nitrogen in the fertiliser that feeds roughly half of humanity, so this is not a chemistry story, it is a food-security story with a carbon problem attached. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — Haber-Bosch is energy-hungry because breaking the nitrogen triple bond needs 400-500°C and 150-200 atmospheres, which is why the plants are enormous, capital-intensive and sited next to cheap natural gas. Electrochemical or low-temperature catalytic routes attack precisely that: if nitrogen can be reduced near ambient conditions, a fertiliser plant stops being a billion-dollar coastal complex and becomes something that can run on a solar farm next to the fields. Establish which catalysts the models identified and by what screening method, what selectivity and current-density figures would be needed to compete (be honest that computational identification is not synthesis, and that the field's history of overstated nitrogen-reduction results makes measured ammonia yields the load-bearing claim — contamination has produced false positives repeatedly), who did the work and where it is published, and what has actually been made in a lab. Then the stakes for our reader: Nigeria, Egypt, Pakistan, Bangladesh and India all import nitrogen fertiliser or the gas to make it, and every fertiliser price shock since 2022 has arrived through that dependency.

stories.label: Brand Hype Has Existed Since the Bronze Age, Scientists Discover
stories.summary: Archaeologists argue that Qurayyah Painted Ware — made in north-west Arabia more than three thousand years ago — meets the working definition of a commodified brand: a distinct visual identity, consistent material recipe, technological continuity across generations, and a reputation that travelled further than the pots did. Lead with the criteria rather than the novelty, because the criteria are the finding: the researchers had to specify what makes a brand a brand before they could test a potsherd against it, and that list is the transferable idea. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — branding is a solution to a trust problem in long-distance trade. When a buyer in the Levant or the Nile Delta cannot inspect a workshop in the Hijaz, a hard-to-fake visual signature substitutes for inspection, and the value of the mark is exactly the cost of forging it. That is the same economics running through waqf-attested craft guilds, hallmarking, and today's certification marks. Establish where Qurayyah is and what the site was, the dating and how it was established, the compositional and petrographic evidence for a single production tradition, how far the ware was traded and what it was traded for, what alternative explanations the authors consider (imitation, prestige emulation, elite gift exchange rather than commerce), and where the paper appeared. Keep the claim exact — the argument is that the ware satisfies a defined set of brand attributes, not that Bronze Age Arabians ran marketing campaigns. Saudi Arabia is an OIC state and no regional outlet carried this in the feed; 404 Media (US) is the sole source, so name the underlying study and its authors.

stories.label: Crypto's next billion users might be AI agents, and they're paying with stablecoins
stories.summary: Coinbase, Cloudflare, MoonPay, Visa and Mastercard are all building rails that let an AI agent spend money inside preset limits — and the unresolved question in every one of them is liability. Lead there rather than on adoption numbers: when an agent overpays, gets prompt-injected into a purchase, or buys from a fraudulent counterparty, no existing framework says whose loss it is, because card chargeback rules assume a human cardholder who can dispute and a merchant who can be reversed. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — this is why stablecoins keep appearing in agent payments. Machine-to-machine commerce wants tiny, instant, final settlement with no per-transaction interchange, and card networks are the exact opposite: batched, reversible, and priced for humans. But finality is the whole problem, because an irreversible payment made by a system that can be talked into things removes the one safety mechanism consumer payments were built around. Establish what each company has actually shipped versus announced, how the spending limits and authorisation scopes work in practice, what x402-style HTTP payment schemes do, real transaction volumes today (adoption is described as nascent — give the number, not the pitch), what a prompt-injected purchase would cost and who eats it under current US and EU rules, and what regulators have said about agent-initiated payments. Then the part our reader should weigh: an agent-payable web is also a web where paywalls, rate limits and API pricing become machine-negotiable, which changes who can afford to read the internet. CoinDesk (US) single-source, reporting on company announcements — attribute the claims to the companies making them.

stories.label: A dumpling shop becomes a poster child of AI adoption in China
stories.summary: A dumpling chain has been elevated into a national example of AI adoption, with its owner quoting Deng Xiaoping — 'science and technology are a primary productive force' — as the justification. Lead with the elevation rather than the technology: the state needs demonstrations that AI has reached the ordinary economy, and a dumpling shop is a better demonstration than a data centre because it implies diffusion. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry, because it is how Chinese industrial policy has always worked and how it is now being applied to AI: designate a model unit, publicise it, and let local officials compete to reproduce it. That produces genuine diffusion and genuine performance — reported adoption outruns actual use, because being seen to adopt is itself the rewarded behaviour. Establish exactly what the shop deployed and what it replaced, whether staff were cut or redeployed and how many, what it cost and who paid, which agency or media amplified it and when, what measurable change in throughput, waste or margin the owner claims and whether anything independent supports it, and how many small firms nationally are reported to have adopted AI tools against any harder indicator. Who bears the cost: the kitchen and counter workers whose tasks are the ones being automated, and who do not appear in the campaign's framing. Then the transferable question for our reader: Gulf states, Indonesia and Pakistan are all running AI-adoption programmes built on showcase deployments, and this is the clearest look at what a showcase actually contains. Rest of World (US) single-source, original on-the-ground reporting from a specialist outlet on technology outside the West.

stories.label: CNES Seeks Partners to Mass-Produce Compact Optical Telescopes
stories.summary: France's space agency has issued an RFI for a compact optical telescope that must be manufacturable in runs exceeding 1,000 units. Lead with that number, because it is the entire strategic content of an otherwise procedural document: space optics have always been hand-built, individually aligned instruments produced in ones and twos, and asking for a thousand declares that Europe intends to field imaging constellations rather than exquisite single satellites. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — the resolution of a space telescope is set by aperture, so a small optic sees less detail; a constellation trades that resolution for revisit rate, meaning you stop asking 'how sharp is the picture' and start asking 'how often do you get one'. For monitoring a border, a port, a fire front or a fleet, revisit beats resolution, and that substitution is why commercial smallsat imaging displaced billion-dollar reconnaissance programmes for most tasks. Establish what the RFI specifies (aperture, spectral bands, mass, ground sample distance) and what it deliberately leaves open, the 18 August publication and the response timeline, which programme it feeds — IRIS² or a French military constellation — and what CNES has said about it, who in Europe can actually mass-produce space optics, and what an equivalent US or Chinese unit costs. Then what this means beyond Europe: mass-produced optics push the price of sovereign Earth observation below the reach of a single wealthy state, which is why Gulf, Turkish and Southeast Asian programmes are the likely export market. European Spaceflight (FR) single-source, a specialist outlet reporting on a public procurement document — cite the RFI itself and its date.

stories.label: US judge strikes down Trump immigrant visa ban affecting 75 countries
stories.summary: Judge Jeannette Vargas voided the suspension not on rights grounds but on statutory authority: the Secretary of State, she found, cannot use a delegated power to build an immigration category Congress never wrote. Lead with the mechanism, because it is the durable part — the ban dies by administrative-law limits, which means it can be rebuilt with different paperwork, and the reader should understand that a win on authority is not a win on principle. Establish exactly which 75 countries were covered and how heavily they skew toward OIC and African states, how many approved petitions were frozen and for how long, what a suspended immigrant visa does to a family already through consular processing, whether the ruling is stayed pending appeal, and what remedy the plaintiffs actually get. Who bears the cost: petitioners in Nigeria, Pakistan, Yemen, Sudan and Afghanistan whose approvals sat unusable. Regional sourcing intact — Al Jazeera (QA) carries the story alongside USA Today (US) and The Independent (GB); sentiment divergence is low at 0.08, so the factual account is not contested, only its framing.

stories.label: US Envoy Warns Israel on Syria Base Attack Near Turkish Border
stories.summary: The US ambassador to Ankara says the intelligence behind Israel's strike on the abandoned Abu al-Duhur air base was simply wrong — Washington found no evidence Türkiye was moving assets there. Lead with what that admission means rather than the strike itself: two US-aligned militaries came within one bad target package of shooting at each other inside a third country, and the only thing that stopped it was an ambassador contradicting an ally in public. Teach the mechanism — northern Syria now has no deconfliction authority that both Israel and Türkiye recognise, so target validation happens unilaterally and the error margin is a war. Establish what Abu al-Duhur is and who actually held it, what Israel said it was striking, what Barrack said and in what forum, whether Türkiye had personnel or equipment anywhere near it, how many Israeli strikes have landed in Syria this month, and the same envoy's separate statement that Israel's Golan occupation runs against UN resolutions and international law — a US official contradicting his own government's recognition. Fold in the further Israeli strike near Damascus that killed occupants of a civilian vehicle, which Damascus is holding Israel responsible for; it is the same campaign, not a second story. Regional sourcing strong: TRT World (TR) primary, with Dawn (PK), The New Arab and Middle East Eye alongside Bloomberg (US) and India Today (IN). Divergence 0.31 — Bloomberg and The New Arab read the same remarks very differently, so quote Barrack directly rather than paraphrasing anyone's framing. Continues the Syria post-regime accounting arc.

stories.label: Ukraine: Russian drone strike hits Kryvyi Rih mall
stories.summary: Sixteen people are now dead at the Sun Gallery shopping centre, and the load-bearing word in the report is 'double-tap' — a second drone timed for the people who arrive after the first. Lead with that pattern, not the toll: a double-tap is not a targeting error, it is a decision to strike rescuers, and it is the specific thing that makes this a war-crimes question rather than a collateral-damage one. Establish how many were killed and injured, how much time separated the two impacts, whether emergency responders were among the dead, what the building was and how full it would have been on a Saturday, what Russia's defence ministry claims it hit in Kryvyi Rih, and what the Geneva Conventions and the Rome Statute say about attacks on those rendering aid. Note that Germany's foreign minister Johann Wadephul was in Kyiv as the toll rose. Single-source (DW) on this specific update — attribute the death toll to Ukrainian emergency services and say so plainly.

stories.label: Sudan Nashra: Burhan offers temporary immunity for internal dialogue participants | AU Peace, Security Council in Khartoum | Khartoum, Riyadh establish bilateral coordination council | Second-largest single group RSF defection arrive in Northern State
stories.summary: Burhan is offering temporary immunity — including suspension of live criminal proceedings — to anyone who joins his intra-Sudanese dialogue, and the immediate beneficiaries are the Sumud opposition leaders currently facing charges. Lead with the trade being made: a transitional authority is buying participation with the one currency it controls, which is prosecution, and that tells you the dialogue's legitimacy problem is legal, not political. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — 'temporary' immunity that expires with the talks makes every participant permanently recallable, so it is leverage dressed as amnesty, and it forecloses accountability for the war's own crimes in the same motion. Establish who exactly is covered and what charges are suspended, how long 'temporary' runs, who has agreed to attend and who has refused, what the AU Peace and Security Council delegation in Khartoum said, what the new Khartoum–Riyadh bilateral coordination council commits either side to, and the scale of the reported RSF defection into Northern State — the second-largest single-group defection so far, which is the clearest battlefield signal in the bulletin. Who bears the cost: Sudanese civilians whose claims against both SAF and RSF sit outside every framework here. Sudan is an OIC state and Mada Masr (EG) is the regional source; note that no Sudanese outlet appears in this feed for the bulletin.

stories.label: China’s Massive New Artificial Island In The South China Sea Emerges, Primed For Militarization
stories.summary: A submerged reef a year ago is now 1,500 acres of dry land with a runway under construction. Lead with the tempo, because it is the argument: twelve months from reef to airstrip means dredging capacity, not legal claim, is what now fixes sovereignty in the South China Sea, and no arbitration timeline moves that fast. Establish which feature this is and whose EEZ it falls in, the acreage and runway length against the earlier Fiery Cross, Subi and Mischief build-outs, what imagery shows of hardened shelters, radar or harbour works, what the 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling actually said about artificial islands generating no maritime entitlement, and what the Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia have said. Who bears the cost: Filipino, Vietnamese and Malaysian fishing fleets whose grounds are enclosed one dredger at a time — Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are OIC states with claims here, and the feed carries no Southeast Asian outlet on this, which is worth auditing feed-side. Satellite-imagery evidence, single-source — attribute the measurements to the imagery analysis and date the images. Fills the China and Southeast Asia gaps the daily audit has flagged.

stories.label: Ukraine Drones Strike Samara Oil Refinery, E-Commerce Warehouse
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones hit a Samara refinery and an Ozon logistics centre while Russia struck fuel tanks and port warehouses at Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi. Lead with the target class, not the exchange: both sides have moved from front-line targets to the civilian logistics that convert fuel and goods into money, because refining and distribution capacity is the one thing neither can replace quickly. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — crude is fungible and refining is not, so a refinery strike does not reduce a country's oil, it strands it; that is why Russia has domestic fuel shortages while still exporting barrels. Establish which Samara plant was hit and its nameplate throughput, how much of Russian refining capacity is now offline across the campaign, what Ozon's warehouse loss means for delivery in the region, what Russia claims it destroyed at the Odesa-region ports, and what a fuel-tank strike does to Ukrainian import logistics. Multi-source with an adversarial pair — Bloomberg (US) and Ukrainska Pravda (UA), divergence 0.03, so the physical facts are broadly agreed; each defence ministry's damage claim should still be attributed, not stated.

stories.label: Russian deputy premier names main sources for dealing with fuel shortages in Russia
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak says Russia will close its fuel gap by importing more and producing lower-class fuel — an official, on the record, in state media. Lead with the second half: dropping to a lower fuel class is a public admission that the shortage is a refining-capacity problem, not a crude problem, because the only reason to sell worse petrol is that you cannot make the good kind. Teach the mechanism — octane and sulphur class are set by secondary units (reformers, hydrotreaters, cat crackers), the exact units drone strikes destroy and the exact units sanctions make hardest to repair, so downgrading the standard is what a refinery-constrained state does instead of rationing. Establish which fuel classes are being relaxed and by what instrument, where the imports come from and at what volume, what the current rationing looks like at the pump and in which regions, how a lower class affects modern engines and emissions, and what Russia's export volumes are doing meanwhile. Who bears the cost: Russian motorists and hauliers, who pay for the war's attrition in engine wear. Advances the Moscow fuel-rationing arc opened on 2026-08-19 with the policy response, distinct from today's strike story. State-media single-source — attribute everything to Novak and to TASS explicitly, and treat the framing as the government's own.

stories.label: Tokenized stocks risk a digital repeat of Wall Street's 'Paperwork Crisis'
stories.summary: The warning is that tokenized equities are rebuilding the 1960s Paperwork Crisis in software: rival venues each issuing their own non-interoperable claim on the same underlying share. Lead with the historical mechanism, because it is the teaching moment — the 1968-70 crisis shut the NYSE on Wednesdays, killed roughly a hundred brokerages, and was solved not by faster clerks but by creating a central depository and dematerialising the certificate. Tokenization inverts that fix: it re-fragments the settlement layer into competing ledgers, and a claim that cannot move between venues is a certificate in a vault again. Establish what a tokenized stock legally is and who holds the real share, how many venues now issue them and on which chains, what happens in a default or corporate action when the token and the register disagree, what the 1960s crisis actually cost, and which regulators have said anything about custody and settlement finality. Who bears the cost: retail holders outside the US buying exposure they cannot redeem. Sourcing note: this is a named-executive interview, so attribute the thesis to Fairmint's CEO and carry the historical record independently.

stories.label: Nigerians turn to faith healers as HIV aid dries up
stories.summary: US aid cuts interrupted free antiretroviral supply in Nigeria, and patients who cannot buy the drugs are being told by unproven 'cures' to stop taking them. Lead with the clinical consequence, not the funding decision: interrupted ART is not the same as untreated HIV — it drives viral rebound and selects for drug-resistant strains, so a break in supply creates a harder epidemic than the one that existed before the programme started. Establish how many Nigerians were on donor-funded ART and how many have missed doses, which programme was cut and when, the price of a month's supply against a median wage, what the resistance data shows about interruption, what NACA and the federal health ministry are doing to bridge, and what the faith healers actually claim and charge. Who holds power: the donor government that switched off a supply chain it had made countries dependent on; who bears the cost: patients whose only visible option is prayer sold at a price. Nigeria is an OIC member and the feed carries no Nigerian outlet on this story — SciDev.Net (GB) is the sole source; flag that gap for feed-side audit. Also answers the audit's note that science has leaned on a single narrow outlet set.

stories.label: ‘Huge Breakthrough’ in the Math of Imbalance
stories.summary: For the first time in thirty years, computer scientists have improved the bound on discrepancy — how evenly a set of objects can be split into two groups. Lead with why a splitting problem is worth thirty years: discrepancy theory is the mathematics of fair division under constraint, and its bounds set the limit on randomised algorithms, experiment design, sampling and load balancing, so an improvement here quietly tightens everything built on them. Establish what the previous bound was and who proved it, what the new result improves it to, whether the proof is constructive (an algorithm you can run) or existential (a guarantee you cannot realise), who the authors are and where the work appeared, and one concrete downstream use — clinical-trial arm assignment or data-centre scheduling — where a better bound changes an actual number. Keep the technical claim exact: state precisely which discrepancy quantity is bounded, since the popular framing 'splitting evenly' loses the whole result. Single-source Quanta (US), a specialist science outlet reporting on published work.

stories.label: Felony charges for citizen deleting phone data at US Border
stories.summary: A US citizen who wiped his phone before a border inspection is facing felony charges — the theory being evidence destruction, applied to a device the government had not yet obtained a warrant for. Lead with the precedent, which is the whole story: if deleting your own data ahead of a warrantless search is a felony, then the border search exception has acquired a duty to preserve, and every traveller now carries an obligation to hand over a device intact. Establish who has been charged and under which statute, exactly what he did and when relative to the inspection, what CBP's warrantless device-search authority actually covers after Riley and the circuit split on forensic searches, how many device searches CBP performed last year, whether any court has upheld this charging theory before, and what the defence argues. Who holds power: the prosecutors choosing to test the theory; who bears the cost: journalists, lawyers and anyone crossing with a client's or source's data on them. Attribute to the New York Times reporting; the story reached the feed via Hacker News at 981 points, a strong public-attention signal from exactly our technical readership.

stories.label: Lawmakers call for investigation into impact of CISA staffing cuts
stories.summary: Lawmakers want a formal investigation because nobody can say what CISA lost — the agency cut staff without any accounting of which capabilities went with them. Lead with that absence: the request is not 'the cuts were too deep', it is 'we have no instrument that would tell us', and an unmeasured reduction in a defensive agency is a risk that only surfaces during an incident. Teach the mechanism — CISA's value is concentrated in threat-hunting teams, the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue, and the federal incident-response bench, all of which are people-shaped and none of which appear on a headcount line, so institutional knowledge leaves without leaving a trace in the budget. Establish how many positions went and from which divisions, who is asking, which oversight body would conduct the review, what CISA has said about backfilling, whether advisory or KEV publication cadence has measurably changed, and what state and local governments — who rely on CISA precisely because they cannot staff this themselves — report. Single-source The Record (US), a specialist security outlet.

stories.label: Usain Bolt's 100m record broken at World Humanoid Robot Games
stories.summary: A humanoid built by Honor — a smartphone maker — ran 100m in 9.32 seconds at 14.5 m/s peak. Lead with who built it, not what it beat: the sprint record is a demonstration that phone-industry supply chains (actuators, batteries, thermal design, volume manufacturing) have reached the point where a consumer-electronics firm can field a competitive bipedal robot, and that is the industrial fact underneath the sports headline. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry — bipedal running is a power-density and control-latency problem, so the number encodes actuator torque-to-weight and control-loop frequency, both of which transfer directly to warehouse and industrial robotics; and be precise that a robot 'beating' Bolt is not a like-for-like comparison, since the machine runs a prepared surface under different rules. Establish the rules and track conditions, what Lightning weighs and what actuators it uses, which other records fell at the Games, how many Chinese firms competed and which state programmes fund them, and what China's humanoid production volumes now look like against US and Japanese output. Sourced by Al Jazeera (QA) and ESPN (US); divergence 0.35 — treat the state-broadcaster timing claim as reported, not verified.
